text: In the Augustan Roman world, Vitruvius describes the chorobates as a straightedge about twenty Roman feet long, supported by matching legs. Plumb lines hanging from the beam indicate level when they simultaneously coincide with vertical lines marked on its crosspieces. He recommends the instrument for surveying the fall along a water-supply route (Book VIII.5.1-2).

text: Vitruvius describes a water reading for the chorobates, a Roman surveying straightedge, when wind makes its plumb lines unsteady. A groove on top of the beam is five feet long, one digit wide and one and a half digits deep in the historical units of his account. Water reaching the groove's rims uniformly indicates level in his description (Book VIII.5.2).
